The build directory is set conditionally based on whether `testsuite.detailed_test_id` is truthy.

```python
self.build_dir = os.path.join(
```

## Changes

**`testinstance.py`** — `TestInstance` now carries toolchain:
- Constructor signature changed to `__init__(self, testsuite, platform, toolchain, outdir)`.
- Stores `self.toolchain`.
- `self.name` is now `platform.name/toolchain/testsuite.name`.
- `build_dir` includes the toolchain segment: `outdir/platform.normalized_name/toolchain/<test_path>` (both the detailed and reconstructed-path branches).

**`testplan.py`** — toolchain-aware planning:
- `apply_filters` iterates `product(ts.integration_toolchains or [None], platform_scope)`, computing the per-instance `toolchain` (the integration toolchain when present, otherwise the environment toolchain, defaulting to `"zephyr"`). This runs for every platform×toolchain combination regardless of `--integration`. The existing `toolchain_allow`/`toolchain_exclude`/`supported_toolchains` filters now use this per-instance value.
- `load_from_file` reads `toolchain` from each serialized suite (falling back to `env.toolchain`) and passes it to `TestInstance`, so restored instances have the attribute and their keys follow `platform/toolchain/name`.
- `add_instances` keys on `instance.name`, which now embeds the toolchain — giving the required `platform_name/toolchain/testsuite_name` key format (and correspondingly toolchain-scoped quarantine/filter lookups).

**`runner.py`** — CMake + logs:
- Adds `-DZEPHYR_TOOLCHAIN_VARIANT=<toolchain>` to the CMake command when set.
- Verbose progress logs append ` <toolchain>`, producing `(handler_type: dut, elapsed_time <toolchain>)` for runs and `(build <toolchain>)` for build-only.

**`reports.py`** — serializes `toolchain` per suite in the test plan JSON.

**`testsuite.py`** — initializes `self.integration_toolchains = []`.

**`testsuite-schema.yaml`** — adds the `integration_toolchains` key (list of strings).
